skills_considered.reason: The discovery ledger is a research surface another batch owns; this wave's question is patient provenance and counting, so findings are proposed through commit candidates instead of ledger edits.
No source in this group tests a therapy against a mechanism; forging hypotheses from single-patient drug histories would manufacture a lead.
No compound is proposed as a candidate; anti-seizure medication histories in case reports are clinical descriptions, not molecules for BLOCK-1 triage.
Scientists do not touch the four current files; changes are proposed as commit candidates for a later BATCH_COMMIT.
No proposed change narrows or reverses a consolidated baseline claim; the triples are published in the candidates for an auditor to run.

entries.proposition: The authors describe the same patient as clinically compatible with Menkes disease and cannot confirm co-pathogenicity.
entries.snippet: This patient also had a significant decrease in blue copper protein, had hair and skin color changes and could have been diagnosed with Menkes disease.

entries.proposition: The authors cannot confirm whether the gene is co-pathogenic.
entries.snippet: We could not confirm whether it was a copathogenic gene.

entries.proposition: The conclusion that WWOX may be associated with poor prognosis rests on this one patient, who also carries the ATP7A variant.
entries.snippet: The genes KCNT1, SCN1A, ALG1, SCN2A, WWOX and ATP7A may be associated with ineffective seizure control and poor prognosis.

entries.proposition: Table 3 records the WWOX patient's seizure control as ineffective while listing oxcarbazepine as effective.
